steps.heading: Prepare your canvas
steps.caption: Start with the printed outline. Protect your table. Use thin coats; rinse and blot your brush between colors.

steps.heading: Turquoise background
steps.caption: Mix turquoise with a little white. Paint around the bouquet and vase with short, loose strokes. Let dry.

steps.heading: Block in the greenery
steps.caption: Mix green with a little brown. Fill leaves and spaces between flowers. Keep the petals, centers and berries white.

steps.heading: Paint the vase bands
steps.caption: Mix blue with a little black for navy. Alternate navy and white bands, starting at the top. Follow the curves; let dry.

steps.heading: Soft blush blooms
steps.caption: Mix white with a little rose red for blush. Fill the upper-left and lower-right blooms. Leave their centers white.

steps.heading: Warm apricot petals
steps.caption: Mix orange with white for apricot. Fill the upper-right flower with curved strokes. Leave its center white.

steps.heading: The rose-red flower
steps.caption: Use rose red for the five central petals. Pull strokes from each petal tip toward the center. Leave the center white.

steps.heading: Golden buds & centers
steps.caption: Mix yellow with a touch of brown for gold. Paint the small buds and all flower centers. Let every base coat dry.

steps.heading: Blend the petals
steps.caption: Shade pink with rose red; apricot with orange; red with rose red + brown. Add white to each for highlights. Feather wet edges with a clean, damp brush.

steps.heading: Leaf & vase highlights
steps.caption: Mix green + yellow for leaf highlights; blue + a little black + white for vase streaks; white + a speck of brown for white-band shadows. Follow the curves.

steps.heading: Berries & final details
steps.caption: Mix blue with a little black for berries. Add white to this mix for shine dots. Shade the yellow centers with brown; dot with yellow and white.

steps.heading: Dry flat & clean up
steps.caption: Let the completed canvas dry lying flat. Wash and reshape brushes, wipe your palette, and close the paint pots.

referenceRestoration.method: Exact deterministic crops from the unchanged canonical working reference; no redraw, overlay, or source replacement.

steps.heading: Prepare the canvas
steps.caption: Start with your printed 8 x 10 canvas. Protect your table. Use thin coats; rinse and blot brushes between colors.

steps.heading: Set the atmosphere
steps.caption: Mix blue, a speck of black and white for a smoky sky. Paint around every outline; leave the shapes white.

steps.heading: Ground & moonlight
steps.caption: Mix brown, a speck of black and a little white for ground. Use white + a little yellow for the moon; paint bats black.

steps.heading: Block in the plum
steps.caption: Mix red and blue with a touch of brown for plum. Paint the hat, brim and coat; keep the band and buckle white.

steps.heading: Add the autumn color
steps.caption: Mix yellow, a little red and a touch of brown for russet orange. Paint pumpkins and band, including buckle center. Leave faces and stems white.

steps.heading: Nose & leather shoes
steps.caption: For peach, mix white, a little yellow and a tiny touch of red. Paint the nose peach and shoes brown.

steps.heading: Shape the beard
steps.caption: Paint beard and mustache white. Mix white with a speck of black and brown for warm gray; pull curved strokes toward the tips.

steps.heading: Finish the base colors
steps.caption: Mix green with a touch of brown for stems. Mix yellow with a touch of brown for the buckle rim. Let dry.

steps.heading: Build depth
steps.caption: Mix red, blue, brown and a speck of black for hat shadows. Mix yellow, a little red and extra brown for pumpkin grooves. Blend softly.

steps.heading: Define the lanterns
steps.caption: Over dry paint, fill the pumpkins' printed eyes and mouths with black using a small brush. Keep the edges controlled.

steps.heading: Catch the light
steps.caption: Mix white with a little yellow for ivory. Add fine, curved highlights to the beard and small shine strokes to the shoes.

steps.heading: Dry & care for tools
steps.caption: Let your canvas dry lying flat. Wash and reshape brushes, wipe the palette and close your paint pots.

referenceRestoration.method: Deterministic canonical crops; removed old drawn brush cues. Step 9 combines a finished-reference hat/fold crop with a resized stage-09 pumpkin-groove crop, without a heavy inset outline or premature black face fill.

inset.note: Canonical step-09 pumpkin grooves; face interiors remain white until step 10.

steps.heading: Start with the outline
steps.caption: Protect your table. Follow the preprinted lines. Keep the background white. Use thin coats; rinse and blot between colors.

steps.heading: Warm orange fur
steps.caption: Paint the head, outer ears, body and lower tail orange. Leave the face patches, chest, tail tip and scarf white.

steps.heading: Soft ivory markings
steps.caption: Mix white with a tiny touch of yellow and brown for ivory. Paint the face patches, inner ears, chest and tail tip.

steps.heading: Forest-green stripes
steps.caption: Mix green with a little brown. Fill alternating printed scarf sections, starting with green at the left of the neck.

steps.heading: Golden scarf stripes
steps.caption: Mix yellow with a little orange. Fill the remaining scarf sections, keeping the printed stripe divisions clear.

steps.heading: Two autumn leaves
steps.caption: Paint the left maple leaf orange. Mix yellow with a little brown for the right oak leaf. Follow each leaf from stem to tip.

steps.heading: Dark paws & features
steps.caption: Mix brown with a little black for the paws and ear tips. Touch up the eyes, nose and smile in black; keep white eye dots.

steps.heading: Layer the fur
steps.caption: Mix orange with a little brown for shadows. Pull short strokes along the cheeks, body and tail; keep lighter orange showing.

steps.heading: Scarf light & shade
steps.caption: Mix green with yellow for light strokes on green stripes. Mix yellow with white for gold highlights. Let base coats dry first.

steps.heading: Leaf veins & tips
steps.caption: Use brown for the printed leaf veins. Mix orange with yellow for maple highlights; add white to yellow for bright oak tips.

steps.heading: Gentle finishing light
steps.caption: Mix white with a touch of brown for soft fur shadows. Add fine white strokes to ivory areas and tiny white eye glints.

steps.heading: Dry & clean up
steps.caption: Lay the canvas flat until fully dry. Wash brushes, wipe the palette and close the paint pots.

steps.heading: Start with the outline
steps.caption: Protect your table. Follow the preprinted lines. Keep the background white. Use thin coats; rinse and blot between colors.

steps.heading: An ivory-white ghost
steps.caption: Mix white with a tiny touch of yellow and brown for ivory. Paint the ghost and hands, keeping the bow, cheeks and pumpkin clear.

steps.heading: Shade the folds
steps.caption: Mix white with a touch of blue and a speck of black. Add soft shadows beside the printed folds; blend into the ivory.

steps.heading: A rich plum bow
steps.caption: Mix red with blue, then a little brown for plum. Paint the bow loops, knot and ribbon tails in thin coats.

steps.heading: The little pumpkin
steps.caption: Paint the pumpkin orange. Follow its curved sections from the stem toward the base; keep the stem and hands clear.

steps.heading: An earthy green stem
steps.caption: Mix green with brown for the stem. Pull small strokes along the bend; add a little yellow to brighten its upper edge.

steps.heading: Warm cheeks & smile
steps.caption: Mix white with a little red and a tiny touch of yellow for peach-pink. Fill the two cheek ovals and the tongue.

steps.heading: Shape the bow folds
steps.caption: Add a little black to the red-blue-brown plum mix for deep folds. Add white to that plum mix for lighter ridge strokes.

steps.heading: Pumpkin ribs & glow
steps.caption: Mix orange with brown for narrow groove shadows. Mix orange with yellow and a little white for curved rib highlights.

steps.heading: Bow-edge highlights
steps.caption: Let the bow dry. Mix red and blue with white for pale purple. Skim the upper bow edges with a lightly loaded small brush.

steps.heading: Brighten the expression
steps.caption: Use black to tidy the eyes and smile. Add tiny white eye dots. Use white along the forehead and hand edges for soft light.

steps.heading: Dry & clean up
steps.caption: Lay the canvas flat until fully dry. Wash brushes, wipe the palette and close the paint pots.

steps.heading: Start with the outline
steps.caption: Protect your table. Follow the preprinted lines. Keep the background white. Use thin coats; rinse and blot between colors.

steps.heading: Orange pumpkin base
steps.caption: Paint the pumpkin shell and rim orange in thin coats. Leave the carved face, opening and kitten white.

steps.heading: Charcoal kitten
steps.caption: Mix black with white and a touch of blue for charcoal gray. Paint the head, paws and curled tail; leave inner ears and nose clear.

steps.heading: Rose ears & nose
steps.caption: Mix white with a little red and a tiny touch of brown for dusty rose. Paint the inner ears, nose and tongue.

steps.heading: Golden eyes
steps.caption: Mix yellow with a little brown for gold. Fill the small curved eye rims; keep the black pupils and white glints distinct.

steps.heading: Deep carved shapes
steps.caption: Mix black with a little brown. Fill the pumpkin eyes, nose and mouth, plus the opening behind the cat. Keep the teeth orange.

steps.heading: Round the pumpkin
steps.caption: Mix orange with brown for the grooves. Mix orange with yellow for rib highlights. Curve each stroke down the pumpkin.

steps.heading: Soft directional fur
steps.caption: Mix white, black and a touch of blue for lighter gray. Pull short strokes over the dry charcoal, following cheeks and tail.

steps.heading: Light along the rim
steps.caption: Mix orange with yellow and a little white. Trace a narrow highlight on the front rim and the upper edges of pumpkin ribs.

steps.heading: Small paw highlights
steps.caption: Mix white with a little black and brown for warm gray. Add short strokes on the paw tops; keep the toe divisions darker.

steps.heading: Whiskers & eye shine
steps.caption: Let the face dry. Use black and a fine brush to tidy whiskers and the smile. Add a small white dot to each eye.

steps.heading: Dry & clean up
steps.caption: Lay the canvas flat until fully dry. Wash brushes, wipe the palette and close the paint pots.

steps.heading: Start with the outline
steps.caption: Protect your table. Follow the preprinted lines. Keep the background white. Use thin coats; rinse and blot between colors.

steps.heading: An even orange base
steps.caption: Paint the pumpkin orange in two thin coats, drying between coats. Leave the stem and carved face white; keep both teeth orange.

steps.heading: Olive-green stem
steps.caption: Mix green with brown for olive. Paint the stem, following its bend. Keep the outer printed contour clear.

steps.heading: The carved smile
steps.caption: Mix black with a little brown. Fill the eyes, nose and mouth carefully around the orange teeth. Let these dark shapes dry.

steps.heading: Shape the grooves
steps.caption: Mix orange with brown for russet shadows. Pull narrow curved strokes beside the printed grooves and around the pumpkin base.

steps.heading: Golden rib highlights
steps.caption: Mix orange with yellow and a little white. Pull lighter strokes down the raised ribs, leaving the shaded grooves visible.

steps.heading: Stem & finishing edges
steps.caption: Mix yellow with brown and a little white for stem highlights. Pull strokes along the bend; tidy carved edges with black and brown.

steps.heading: Dry & clean up
steps.caption: Lay the canvas flat until fully dry. Wash brushes, wipe the palette and close the paint pots.

steps.heading: Set up your canvas
steps.caption: Cover your table. Follow the printed outlines. Rinse and blot your brush between colors.

steps.heading: Paint the background
steps.caption: Mix white with a touch of blue for the sky. Paint snow white. Work around printed shapes.

steps.heading: Paint the trees
steps.caption: Paint trees green; keep lights white. Mix green + blue + white for the small distant tree. Use downward strokes; add green + yellow highlights.

steps.heading: Paint hat and coat
steps.caption: Use red in thin layers. Leave the nose, beard, pom-pom and light circles white.

steps.heading: Add nose and shoes
steps.caption: For peach, mix white, a little yellow and a tiny touch of red. Paint the nose peach and the shoes brown.

steps.heading: Paint the fluffy whites
steps.caption: Paint beard and pom-pom white. For shadows, mix white, a touch of blue and a speck of black.

steps.heading: Shape the hat folds
steps.caption: Mix red with a little brown for shadows. Blend along the hat folds. Add red with a touch of yellow for highlights. Let dry.

steps.heading: Light up the hat
steps.caption: Paint bulbs yellow over a dry white base. Add white shine dots. Use green and a speck of black for the cord.

steps.heading: Paint the tree lights
steps.caption: Use blue and yellow. Let dry, then add tiny white dots to make the ornaments shine.

steps.heading: Brighten the snow
steps.caption: Mix white with a touch of blue for snow shadows. Add white highlights to snow and beard.

steps.heading: Refine the pom-pom
steps.caption: Dab white over the pom-pom's blue shadows. Let dry before fixing edges. Add a few white snow dots to the hat if you like.

steps.heading: Let it dry
steps.caption: Lay your canvas flat until dry. Wash brushes, close paint pots and clean your palette.

steps.heading: Begin with the outline
steps.caption: Protect your table. Follow the printed lines; use thin coats. Rinse and blot brushes between colors.

steps.heading: Brush in the teal sky
steps.caption: Mix teal with a little white. Paint with short strokes. Add yellow wind highlights.

steps.heading: Ground & branches
steps.caption: Paint branches and stems brown. Mix green with a little brown for the ground; leave leaves white.

steps.heading: Fill the curling hat
steps.caption: Mix red with a little brown for rust. Paint thin curved strokes that follow the folds.

steps.heading: Sleeves & leather
steps.caption: Mix green with a little brown for sleeves. Paint boots brown; add a speck of black along lower edges.

steps.heading: Lay in autumn color
steps.caption: Mix orange with a touch of brown for pumpkins and the maple leaf. Alternate orange and yellow on other leaves.

steps.heading: Skin & soft beard
steps.caption: For peach, mix white, a little yellow and a tiny touch of red. Paint nose and hands. Mix white with a touch of yellow for the beard.

steps.heading: Light the lanterns
steps.caption: Paint frames, chains and rings black + a little brown. Use yellow in the glass; add white to yellow for flames and a soft glow.

steps.heading: Shape the hat
steps.caption: Mix red, brown and a speck of black for fold shadows. Mix red with a little yellow for highlights. Blend along curves.

steps.heading: Round the pumpkins
steps.caption: Mix orange with brown for groove shadows. Mix orange with a little yellow for highlights; follow the ribs.

steps.heading: Pull fine beard strands
steps.caption: Mix white, a touch of teal and a speck of brown for shadows. Pull strokes toward the tips; add white and a little yellow highlights.

steps.heading: Dry & clean up
steps.caption: Let the canvas dry flat. Wash and reshape brushes, wipe the palette and close paint pots.

steps.heading: Set up
steps.caption: Cover the table. Start with the printed outline. Use thin coats; rinse and blot brushes between colors.

steps.heading: Blend the sky
steps.caption: Mix white with blue for the upper sky. Below, blend yellow into orange, then red plus white. Work horizontally around the outlines.

steps.heading: Light the sunset
steps.caption: Mix white with yellow for the sun and bright cloud streaks. Mix white with red for softer streaks. Let the sky dry.

steps.heading: Layer distant ridges
steps.caption: Mix blue with white for the far ridges. Use less white in each nearer ridge. Follow the printed curves; let adjoining bands dry.

steps.heading: Deepen the valley
steps.caption: Mix blue with green and a little black. Fill the nearest forest slopes. Tap upward with the small brush for pointed treetops.

steps.heading: Block in the rocks
steps.caption: Mix black, brown and a little white. Brush this gray-brown base across the rock slabs. Leave the printed fallen leaves white.

steps.heading: Paint the tree
steps.caption: Mix brown with a little black. Fill the trunk and branches with lengthwise strokes. Keep the foliage white. Let the base dry.

steps.heading: Build autumn color
steps.caption: Mix red with a little brown. Dab into the canopy and shrubs. Add orange over most areas, leaving darker pockets visible.

steps.heading: Lift the leaves
steps.caption: Mix orange with yellow. Tap small clusters along the lit foliage edges, leaving gaps. Use red, orange and yellow on fallen leaves.

steps.heading: Catch the bark light
steps.caption: Mix brown with yellow and a little white. Drag a nearly dry small brush along the trunk's left edge and branch tops.

steps.heading: Define the ledges
steps.caption: Mix white with a little black and brown. Skim the upper rock edges with a nearly dry brush. Keep the dark cracks visible.

steps.heading: Dry and clean up
steps.caption: Lay the canvas flat until fully dry. Wash and reshape brushes, wipe the palette and close the paint pots.

steps.heading: Prepare your space
steps.caption: Protect your table. Follow the preprinted lines. Use thin coats; rinse and blot brushes between colors.

steps.heading: Lay in the sky
steps.caption: Mix blue with a little black. Paint only the sky around the flowers and greenery. Keep all plant shapes white.

steps.heading: Turn the blue swirls
steps.caption: Mix blue with white. Follow the sky curves with short strokes, leaving darker gaps. Let dry.

steps.heading: Light the stars
steps.caption: Mix white with a little yellow. Dab star centers and curved light trails. Keep some blue showing.

steps.heading: Paint both flowers
steps.caption: Paint every petal yellow, from its base toward its tip. Keep seed heads and greenery white. Let dry.

steps.heading: Warm the folds
steps.caption: Brush orange along petal bases and one side of each fold. Blend into yellow with outward strokes.

steps.heading: Paint stems and leaves
steps.caption: Mix green with a little blue. Fill stems, leaves and curled flower backs, following their length.

steps.heading: Fill the seed heads
steps.caption: Mix brown with a little black. Fill both seed heads; use small dabs along the rims. Let dry.

steps.heading: Shape the greenery
steps.caption: Mix green with yellow for light edges. Mix green with blue and a speck of black for shadows. Pull curved strokes.

steps.heading: Lift the petals
steps.caption: Mix yellow with a little white. Pull slender highlights from base to tip on dry petals; leave orange folds visible.

steps.heading: Stipple the seeds
steps.caption: Dab brown, orange and yellow onto dry seed heads. Mix white with yellow for a few bright dots. Keep dark gaps.

steps.heading: Dry and clean up
steps.caption: Lay the canvas flat until fully dry. Wash and reshape brushes, wipe the palette and close the paint pots.
